aspect: Three sides, three queues, three sets of rules
description: The Palestinian side at Jericho, the Israeli side at Allenby, the Jordanian side at King Hussein. Each has its own procedures and its own capacity to stop you, and clearing one says nothing about the next.
energy_note: Cleared three times, refused once, and that's the trip.

aspect: EXAMPLE - September 2025, closed indefinitely with no notice
description: Israel abruptly closed the crossing, stranding Palestinians abroad, forcing patients being treated in Jordan to extend their stays, and separating families. It announced reopening to foot traffic only the following day.
money_note: Extended hotel and treatment costs while stranded.
energy_note: Locked out of your own country on a Wednesday.

aspect: Being stranded abroad is the expensive direction
description: When it closes while you are outside, the costs run: accommodation, missed work, rebooked flights, a visa in the transit country that may expire, and no date at which any of it ends.
energy_note: A closure with no end date, and you are on the wrong side.

description: Travel insurance does not cover a border closure by the occupying power, and airlines do not treat it as a disruption they caused. The loss sits entirely with the traveller.

Her mother's oncology follow-up is in Amman because the machine in Nablus has been waiting on a part for seven months. They cross on the Sunday. On the Tuesday the bridge closes. The follow-up becomes eleven days in a cousin's flat, and the appointment after it is missed entirely.
energy_note: A cancer schedule, kept by a border guard.
